memory_line: Promethazine: dilute, drip, big vein. Never push.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 2:10 AM. She's 68, nauseated after gallbladder surgery. Promethazine 12.5 mg IV (intravenous) as needed. Her only IV is in her hand.

❌ 3 mistakes, 3 error types
1️⃣ Knowledge gap: pushed it undiluted. The label changed in 2023
2️⃣ Missed keyword: into a hand vein, which the label rules out
3️⃣ Acted too late: "It burns!" and the nurse kept pushing
➡️ 6:30 AM: her hand pale, cold, fingers dusky. Urgent surgery consult.

💉 Promethazine IV (NEVER PUSH IT)
• It can damage tissue badly if it leaks from the vein or enters an artery
• Injuries have included gangrene and amputation
• Deep IM (intramuscular) is the preferred route

✅ The right move
• Ask whether IM, or another antiemetic, is an option
• IV only if needed: dilute in normal saline (1 mg/mL or less) and infuse over 20 to 40 minutes, per the label
• A large vein, ideally central. Never the hand or wrist
• Burning or pain: stop now and report

🧠 Promethazine: dilute, drip, big vein. Never push.

rn_checks: FDA Dec 2023 labeling: deep IM preferred; IV only after dilution in 0.9% sodium chloride (contraindicated IV above 1 mg/mL; adult 12.5 to 50 mg in 50 mL), infused over 20 to 40 minutes through a large vein, preferably central; never through IV catheters in the hand or wrist; label: stop the infusion right away for pain or burning
Boxed warning: severe tissue injury including gangrene, regardless of route
